video_title: Training Camp Media Availability | October 4, 2026 | OKC Thunder

quotes.speaker: AJ
quotes.summary_phrase: AJ on feeling more comfortable entering his third training camp
quotes.excerpt: Definitely feel more comfortable, obviously know how it goes now. Really excited to get the season started.
quotes.quote: Definitely feel more comfortable, obviously know how it goes now. Really excited to get the season started. We have a very competitive group and it's been really fun.
quotes.social_post: AJ says he feels much more comfortable entering his third training camp with the Thunder. He notes the group is very competitive and he is excited to get the season started.

quotes.speaker: AJ
quotes.summary_phrase: AJ on his focus for the upcoming season
quotes.excerpt: Just being where my feet are, just being focused on the task ahead.
quotes.quote: Just being where my feet are, just being focused on the task ahead. For me it's just getting better every day and as a team, us getting better every day. If we take that approach we will be just fine.
quotes.social_post: AJ on his mindset for the upcoming season: Just being where my feet are and focused on the task ahead. He says the goal is simply getting better every day as a team.

quotes.speaker: AJ
quotes.summary_phrase: AJ on Kenrich Williams' competitive nature
quotes.excerpt: Kenrich Williams has been here for a while, he's one of our leaders and every time we play he's competitive.
quotes.quote: Kenrich Williams has been here for a while, he's one of our leaders and every time we play he's competitive. Whatever it is, one-on-one, shooting drill, he's competitive in everything and I think that brings the best out of all of us, so it's great to have him.
quotes.social_post: AJ praises Kenrich Williams for his competitive nature, saying he brings the best out of everyone on the Thunder roster during drills and practice.

quotes.speaker: AJ
quotes.summary_phrase: AJ on Kenrich Williams' winning mentality
quotes.excerpt: He's a winner. Every time he's out there he's competing, offense, defense, he's going to give everything.
quotes.quote: He's a winner. Every time he's out there he's competing, offense, defense, he's going to give everything out there and I think that's an example for all our guys.
quotes.social_post: AJ calls Kenrich Williams a winner who sets an example for the rest of the team with his constant effort on both ends of the floor.

quotes.speaker: AJ
quotes.summary_phrase: AJ on his defensive development and learning from teammates
quotes.excerpt: Being part of a team that's so good defensively. We had great guys like Lou, AC, Cason, Dub.
quotes.quote: Being part of a team that's so good defensively. We had great guys like Lou, AC, Cason, Dub. We have great defensive players and that helped me just to learn from them. Me learning the game, getting stronger, I think all that helps and just being a competitor. At the end of the day it comes down to competing and every time I'm on the court I want to compete.
quotes.social_post: AJ credits his defensive development to learning from teammates like Lu Dort, Alex Caruso, Cason Wallace, and Jalen Williams.

quotes.speaker: AJ
quotes.summary_phrase: AJ on the impact of having multiple offensive creators
quotes.excerpt: Having a lot of guys that can handle the ball, make decisions, just opens the floor for everyone.
quotes.quote: Having a lot of guys that can handle the ball, make decisions, just opens the floor for everyone else, so it's great.
quotes.social_post: AJ says having multiple offensive creators on the Thunder roster is a major advantage because it opens up the floor for everyone else.

quotes.speaker: Unidentified speaker
quotes.summary_phrase: Coach on the team's approach to the condensed preseason schedule
quotes.excerpt: We make our own preseason schedule so the back-to-backs are actually by design.
quotes.quote: We make our own preseason schedule so the back-to-backs are actually by design. We're not going to play everybody in every game. At least the high-minute rotation guys, we will play some guys five games, but the high-minute guys won't play in every game and so condensing it actually gives us more practice time on either end of those games.
quotes.social_post: Thunder coach says the team's preseason back-to-backs are by design. High-minute rotation players will not play in every game to allow for more practice time.

quotes.speaker: Unidentified speaker
quotes.summary_phrase: Coach on balancing player needs for experience and preparation
quotes.excerpt: Some people need experience and game time and some people just need a bare minimum.
quotes.quote: We're just trying to get everybody what they need. Some people need experience and game time and some people just need a bare minimum to get themselves ready for the season.
quotes.social_post: The Thunder coaching staff is balancing preseason minutes by giving younger players the experience they need while ensuring veterans get the bare minimum to be ready.

quotes.speaker: Unidentified speaker
quotes.summary_phrase: Coach on the importance of preseason travel for rookies
quotes.excerpt: They need to play five games and they need to deal with the recovery of that.
quotes.quote: They need to play five games and they need to deal with the recovery of that and the higher minutes of that, and that gives them a valuable experience they can get a lot better from that, whereas guys that have been through that in NBA seasons don't need the exposure to that in September, October.
quotes.social_post: Thunder coach explains that rookies need the five-game preseason experience to handle recovery and higher minutes, while veterans do not need that exposure.

quotes.speaker: Unidentified speaker
quotes.excerpt: It professionalizes the segment of practice that they're covering.
quotes.quote: It professionalizes the segment of practice that they're covering. If you tell them to manage it like a game, it's going to feel like a game and we try to take advantage of that because it just gives us some exposure to that type of environment before we actually get into it in the preseason games.
quotes.social_post: Thunder coach says the team tries to professionalize practice segments by managing them like games to get players ready for the environment of the regular season.

quotes.speaker: Unidentified speaker
quotes.summary_phrase: Coach on the team's philosophy of teaching to the fastest learner
quotes.excerpt: We teach to the fastest learner, not the slowest.
quotes.quote: We teach to the fastest learner, not the slowest and so we're trying to pace with the guys that have experience and it's their job to use the extra time and extra resources to try to catch up to that.
quotes.social_post: Thunder coach on the team's teaching philosophy: We teach to the fastest learner, not the slowest. He says it is the job of less experienced players to use extra resources to catch up.

quotes.speaker: Unidentified speaker
quotes.summary_phrase: Coach on the value of playing preseason games in Oklahoma
quotes.excerpt: We're the professional sports team in the state, so we're grateful for our fans.
quotes.quote: We understand we're the state of Oklahoma's team and we're the professional sports team in the state, so we're grateful for our fans certainly in the city, but all around the state and going up to that market allows us to get in front of those fans and show them our appreciation.
quotes.social_post: Thunder coach says playing preseason games around the state of Oklahoma is a priority to show appreciation for the team's fans outside of Oklahoma City.

quotes.speaker: Unidentified speaker
quotes.summary_phrase: Coach on Shai Gilgeous-Alexander's professionalism and experience
quotes.excerpt: He's so experienced at this point that he understands what he needs in camp.
quotes.quote: He's so experienced at this point that he understands what he needs in camp and he gets what he needs. Most of those guys are like that. Kenrich is like that, Caruso is like that, I think Dub is probably at that point, Chet, these guys, they kind of know what they need and how they get it and so he's very professional with that. He gets what he needs, no more. He knows what's coming, he's got great perspective, he handles all the stages of the season very well.
quotes.social_post: Thunder coach praises Shai Gilgeous-Alexander for his professionalism, noting that he knows exactly what he needs to prepare for the season and handles the stages of the year well.
